All twelve behaviours are settled and recorded. Here's the **full scope** we've shaped together — please review it as the thing I'd build.

## Scope summary — your personal bookmark app

**Saving**
1. Paste a link (even without `https://` — it's completed for you) and save it after a quick review of its auto-fetched title, description, site icon, and preview image, which you can correct first.
2. Re-saving the same link doesn't duplicate it — it opens the existing one; "same link" is judged safely (ignoring only capitalisation of the site and a harmless trailing slash).
3. Edit a bookmark's title, description, and address later; the address must be a valid web link.

**Finding**
4. Instant search as you type, across title, description, address, and notes — with quoted exact phrases, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, grouping, and `#tag` matching real tags.

**Read-later**
5. A deliberate "Read later" queue (opt-in when saving) with All / To read / Read filters and a per-item toggle; opening a link never auto-marks it.

**Organising**
6. Tags (several per link), shown on cards, clickable to filter, with existing-tag suggestions as you type.

**Managing**
7. Reversible **Archive** and permanent **Delete** (confirmed), tucked in a ⋯ menu.
8. **Notes** with simple Markdown — plain preview on the card, full formatted read-only view.
9. **Bulk actions** on many selected links: reading state, archive/restore, add/remove a tag, delete; "Select all" spans the whole filtered set.
10. **Saved views**: named search + include/exclude tags + filter + sort, recomputed live.
11. **Preserve a page**: an on-demand self-contained copy (the PDF itself when it's a PDF), plus an optional Internet Archive link.
12. **Import/Export**: full JSON backup and browser-standard HTML (flat, with tags & dates); import merges and skips duplicates.

**Comfort & settings**
- Sort (newest/oldest/title), "Load more" paging, and text size — all remembered as preferences.

**What becomes real in the build (simulated in the prototype):**
- Your bookmarks **and** settings **sync across your devices** via a personal account (not just one browser).
- Real page/PDF fetching — including deciding a **PDF by its actual file type**, not the address — and real Internet Archive submission.

I've also recorded a few ideas you raised for **later** (not in this build): an explicit "refresh page details" action when you repoint an address.

That's the whole scope. **May I now switch from exploring to building this for real?** Once you approve, I'll move into development.
